title: Nutrition and Diet
hook: Your body runs on food, but not all food does the same job — different food groups supply the fuel, building blocks, and protection your cells need.
key_points: Nutrition is how the body takes in and uses the nutrients in food.
A balanced diet draws from several food groups, each with a different role.
Carbohydrates and fats supply energy; proteins build and repair tissue.
Fruits and vegetables provide vitamins, minerals, and fiber.
content_html: Nutrition is how your body takes in food and turns it into everything it needs — energy to move, raw materials to grow and repair, and the small helpers that keep its chemistry running. No single food does it all, which is why a healthy diet pulls from several food groups, each playing a distinct role.
extra_html: The USDA's MyPlate guide sorts food into a few key groups: fruits, vegetables, grains, protein foods, and dairy. Carbohydrates from grains and fruit are the body's go-to energy source, while fats supply concentrated, longer-lasting energy. Proteins — from beans, eggs, fish, and meat — provide the amino acids used to build and repair tissue. Fruits and vegetables deliver vitamins, minerals, and fiber that keep systems working smoothly. The MyPlate message is simple: fill half your plate with fruits and vegetables and vary what you eat, because balance across the groups is what gives the body the full mix it depends on.

related.title: Vitamins and Minerals
related.hook: Needed in only tiny amounts, vitamins and minerals are the micronutrients that quietly run reactions your body can't manage without.

related.title: The Digestive System
related.hook: From the first bite to the final absorption, your digestive tract is a one-way assembly line that turns food into fuel your cells can use.

related.title: Diet and Disease
related.hook: What you eat over years quietly shapes your odds of heart disease, type 2 diabetes, and more — diet is one of the strongest levers on long-term health.

flashcards.back_html: Eating from a variety of food groups — fruits, vegetables, grains, protein foods, and dairy — so the body gets the energy and nutrients it needs.

flashcards.prompt: Which food group is the body's main source of quick energy?

choices.text: Carbohydrates, like grains, bread, and fruit

flashcards.explanation_html: Carbohydrates break down into sugars the body burns for energy. Grains, fruits, and starchy vegetables are rich sources.

flashcards.prompt: What is the main job of protein in the diet?

choices.text: Building and repairing tissues like muscle

flashcards.explanation_html: Proteins supply amino acids — the building blocks the body uses to grow, maintain, and repair tissues such as muscle.
